Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: every wrong submission costs 1 and every demo request costs 1. An
instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

description: Continual-ARC puzzle instances: reuse task programs, learn from demos, validate transforms, and submit grids.

# Continual-ARC

1. At each instance start, check `programs/<task id>.py` before requesting demos. If present, run its `transform(grid)` on the test input and submit that exact result first.
2. If the file is absent or its submitted answer is incorrect, request demonstrations only as needed. Infer output colors and unchanged cells from examples; do not add arbitrary count, color, or shape thresholds unsupported by them. Implement or revise `transform(grid)`, then run it on every exact received pair and require full-grid equality—not spot checks—before submitting its generated test result. Serialize that result directly from the program and validate it is a rectangular grid of 1–30 rows and columns with integer cells 0–9; submit the serialized output verbatim rather than manually retyping it.
3. After the verdict, save the transform that reproduces all received pairs to the task file, replacing an older version, then finish once the instance is over.
4. On every response to the ARC instance—including after feedback or tool work—choose exactly one permitted action (`submit`, `request_demos`, or `finish`) and make the entire reply that JSON object; tool calls or file edits are not actions. Never submit a hand-authored grid that was not produced by the task program.
